channel.title: Weekfold
channel.description: The world's week, folded into one free edition every Sunday.

item.title: Brazil votes in knife-edge runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Final polls show a near dead heat as nearly 160 million eligible voters choose between the veteran president and the son of the jailed ex-president.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march across France as nearly 1,000 are arrested
item.description: A week after rioting and looting, Saturday's protests over living costs passed with clashes in several cities under a 70,000-strong police deployment.

item.title: Israel locks down Hebron after attack kills two soldiers days before election
item.description: Netanyahu ordered the West Bank city sealed and prepared wider closures as the army launched a multi-day operation and arrests mounted.

item.title: Iran says seven ships hit in Hormuz as US and Europe weigh next move
item.description: The Revolutionary Guard's claim of its highest single-day toll in the strait is disputed by the US, while ministers urge diplomacy and Washington hints at strikes.

item.title: Oslo talks on Ukraine end without a deal as Witkoff heads to Putin
item.description: Zelenskyy met US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Norway, with Washington calling the talks constructive but no agreement reached.

item.title: Drone strike on Abyei market kills at least 153 people
item.description: The toll from Monday's attack in the disputed Sudan-South Sudan border zone more than doubled as fires slowed recovery of bodies.

item.title: Kenyan cult leader convicted over starvation deaths of 190 children
item.description: A Mombasa court found preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 others guilty of murder over the Shakahola Forest deaths, with sentencing set for 6 November.

item.title: Xenophobic violence in South Africa prompts African artists to withdraw from performances
item.description: Escalating attacks on migrants in South Africa prompted prominent African musicians to cancel or reschedule performances, including Malian artist Salif Keita and South African singer Tyla.

item.title: Student protests over education and governance spread across three continents
item.description: Student-led demonstrations that began in France over education policy have spread to Albania and Argentina, where protesters demand the resignation of leaders and oppose cuts to public services.

item.title: School shooting in Oregon kills four; teen suspect shot by community member
item.description: A 16-year-old opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon on Friday, killing three children and a teacher before an armed community member shot and killed the suspect.

item.title: Russia intensifies Ukraine attacks as Trump claim of ceasefire falls apart
item.description: Russian drone strikes killed at least nine civilians in Ukraine on Wednesday, leaving hundreds of thousands without power. President Zelensky said he felt betrayed by Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire neither side supports.

item.title: China's Pinglu Canal opens to reshape Asian trade routes
item.description: China inaugurated the $11 billion Pinglu Canal, a 134-kilometer waterway linking southwestern China to the Beibu Gulf and Southeast Asia, shortening shipping times and reducing costs for the region's largest trade partner.

item.title: Iran's navy strikes tanker in Strait of Hormuz amid shipping chaos
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for striking a third tanker in two days in the Strait of Hormuz, as cargo ships face mounting attacks threatening global trade.

item.title: Houthis strike Saudi airport for third time in as many days
item.description: A Houthi missile hit the passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Monday, killing one person and forcing operations to suspend after a strike a day earlier left at least 12 dead.

item.title: Pakistan imposes emergency rule on Imran Khan's last stronghold
item.description: Islamabad suspended the PTI-run government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and put the province under its governor, citing failures against militancy.

item.title: Missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and wounds over 300
item.description: A projectile hit a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport, the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, as Yemen's war spreads.

item.title: Navi Pillay, champion of international justice, wins Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: The 85-year-old South African jurist was honoured for decades of work making sure war crimes and genocide are prosecuted.

item.title: US freezes green-card sponsorship for eight tech and IT giants
item.description: The Labor Department has stopped accepting or processing permanent labour certifications from Microsoft, Adobe and six major IT outsourcing firms, citing alleged abuse of immigration rules.

item.title: Russian missile barrage kills dozens in Ukraine, flattening Pryluky apartments
item.description: Seventy missiles and dozens of drones hit Ukraine overnight, and a strike on a five-storey building in Pryluky killed 22 people, five of them children.

item.title: IceCube founder Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in Physics
item.description: The Belgian-born physicist is honoured for leading the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole and for detecting high-energy neutrinos from deep space.

item.title: Optogenetics pioneers win Nobel medicine prize for light-controlled neurons
item.description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel share the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering a light-activated molecular switch that lets scientists turn individual nerve cells on and off.

item.title: Brazil heads to Lula-Bolsonaro runoff as the right surges
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro took about 47% to President Lula's 45% in the first round, setting up a 25 October runoff.

item.title: UAE calls FlyDubai cockpit axe attack an act of terrorism
item.description: A co-pilot struck the captain with the crash axe on a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight; passengers subdued him and the jet landed safely in Saudi Arabia.

item.title: US hiring nearly stalls with just 29,000 jobs in September
item.description: Payroll growth missed forecasts, earlier months were revised down by 60,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2%.

item.title: Russian drones hit Kyiv's Southern Bridge, halting metro across Dnipro
item.description: Two drones struck near the supports of the cable-stayed bridge, the first drone attack on one of the capital's river crossings.

item.title: Last US troops leave Iraq, closing the anti-ISIS mission
item.description: American and coalition forces completed their departure from Erbil Air Base, ending Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq after 12 years.

item.title: Iran sends Hormuz reopening plan to Washington via Qatar
item.description: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Qatari mediators in New York and said he expected a US answer within a day, while Washington insisted any deal must cover Iran's nuclear programme.

item.title: Myanmar jet bombs busy Rakhine market, killing dozens of civilians
item.description: A military air strike near the main wholesale market in Kyauktaw, in rebel-held Rakhine state, killed at least 33 people, a toll that later rose to 49.
